title: VISION-3D: Virtual Imaging of Sarcoma: Interdisciplinary preOperative plaNning using 3D models
summary: VISION-3D is a clinical study aiming to improve surgical planning for soft tissue sarcomas (rare and complex tumors). The goal is to determine whether using virtual reality headsets and interactive 3D models of a patient's anatomy can enhance preoperative planning. Participants are randomly assigned to a control group (standard 2D planning) or an intervention group (3D-VR planning). The study evaluates whether this approach can reduce surgery time, increase planning accuracy, and lower complication rates.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of other connective and soft tissue

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosis of a soft tissue sarcoma (abdominal, retroperitoneal, thoracic, or extremity)
- Tumor size > cT1
- Locally resectable tumor (isolated or oligometastatic)
- Written informed consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
- Emergency procedures
- Time-critical indications that do not allow adequate preoperative planning (<48 hours until surgery)
- Re-resections following R1/R2 resections
- Purely diagnostic procedures (e.g., histological confirmation/incisional biopsies)
- Change of the designated surgeon shortly before the operation
